test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 15 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: What was the total central government receipts (excluding borrowings) estimated at the Union Budget 2025-26?
solution:
The correct answer is __**₹34.96 lakh crore**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Union Budget 2025-26**, presented by the Union Minister for Finance and Corporate Affairs, **Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman**, on **February 1, 2025**, estimated the total receipts of the Central Government (excluding borrowings) at **₹34.96 lakh crore**.
 
• These receipts primarily comprise **Revenue Receipts** and **Non-Debt Capital Receipts**. Revenue receipts are further divided into **Tax Revenue** (Net to Centre) and **Non-Tax Revenue**.
 
• For the financial year **2025-26**, the **Tax Receipts (Net to Centre)** are estimated at **₹28.40 lakh crore**, showing a robust growth in tax collections compared to the previous financial year. ***Hence, the statement regarding receipts is correct.***
 
• The **Non-Tax Revenue** is estimated at **₹5.96 lakh crore**, which includes dividends from the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** and Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs), along with interest receipts.
 
• The **Non-Debt Capital Receipts** (which include recovery of loans and disinvestment proceeds) are estimated at **₹0.60 lakh crore**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Total Expenditure:** The total expenditure for the financial year **2025-26** is estimated at **₹51.21 lakh crore**. This indicates a significant investment in social sectors and infrastructure to achieve the goal of **Viksit Bharat by 2047**.
 
• **Capital Expenditure (Capex):** The government has continued its focus on infrastructure by proposing a capital expenditure outlay of **₹11.41 lakh crore**. This represents approximately **3.4% of the GDP**, aimed at creating long-term assets and generating employment.
 
• **Fiscal Deficit:** The **Fiscal Deficit** for **2025-26** is estimated at **4.3% of the GDP**. The government remains committed to its fiscal consolidation path, aiming to reduce the deficit below **4.5%** in the coming years.
 
• **Revenue Deficit:** The **Revenue Deficit** is projected at **1.4% of the GDP** for **2025-26**, reflecting the government's effort to balance consumption expenditure with revenue generation.
 
• **Gross Market Borrowings:** To bridge the gap between receipts and expenditure, the **Gross Market Borrowings** through dated securities for **2025-26** are estimated at **₹15.22 lakh crore**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Major Allocation Sectors:** The **Budget 2025-26** prioritizes **Agriculture**, **Employment**, **Human Resource Development**, and **Social Justice**. Significant funds are allocated to the **PM-Kisan scheme** and **MNREGA** to support the rural economy.
 
• **Direct Tax Reforms:** The budget introduced changes in the **New Tax Regime**, increasing the standard deduction and adjusting tax slabs to provide relief to the middle class and salaried individuals.
 
• **Indirect Taxes:** Rationalization of **Customs Duties** on various items like gold, silver, and critical minerals was announced to promote domestic manufacturing and value addition under the **Make in India** initiative.
 
• **Health and Education:** The allocation for **Health** and **Education** saw an increase to strengthen the **National Health Mission** and the **Samagra Shiksha Abhiyan**, ensuring holistic development.
